description: Architectural fitness rules for Codebase Cortex. Every rule traces to the ADR whose invariant it enforces, so a failure names the decision and (via docs/adr/ + .github/CODEOWNERS) the maintainer who owns it. Edit this file to add a rule; the check scripts contain no repository-specific knowledge.

import_boundaries.description: Layering rules. Each rule names a set of files (scope) and the modules those files may not import (forbid).

layer_rules.description: The domain core is the innermost layer; dependencies point inwards only.
layer_rules.message: src/core/ must not import the edge layer ({module}). Dependencies point inwards: move the shared type into src/core/ or invert the call with a port. [{adr}]

layer_rules.description: Domain logic stays framework-agnostic so it is testable and transport-independent.
layer_rules.message: src/core/ must not depend on a web framework ({module}). Raise a domain error and let the edge layer translate it to HTTP. [{adr}]

layer_rules.description: ADR-002 makes the shared Redis cache a single layer; other layers depend on its interface, never on the driver.
layer_rules.message: Only src/cache/ may talk to Redis directly ({module}). Depend on the src.cache session-store interface so the shared cache layer stays swappable. [{adr}]

layer_rules.description: ADR-003 requires billing and notification side-effects to travel over the event bus, not the request stack.
layer_rules.message: The request layer must not import a side-effect implementation ({module}). Publish an event on src.events.bus and let an asynchronous consumer do the work. [{adr}]

banned_dependencies.description: Banned imports, banned call sites, and in-process state that would silently break an ADR invariant.

banned_modules.description: In-process cache libraries keep state in the worker's heap, which is exactly what ADR-002 forbids.
banned_modules.message: {module} keeps cached state inside the process; ADR-002 requires session state and token blacklists to live in the shared Redis cache layer, which survives a pod restart. [{adr}]

banned_modules.description: A synchronous transport in a billing or notification path re-creates the cascade-timeout failure ADR-003 was written to remove.
banned_modules.message: {module} is a blocking transport. ADR-003 requires billing and notification side-effects to be emitted as events and retried asynchronously with exponential backoff. [{adr}]

banned_calls.description: Catches a blocking outbound call even when the transport was imported under an alias or re-exported.
banned_calls.message: {call}() blocks the user-facing request on a third-party call. ADR-003: emit the event and return; a consumer performs the side-effect with retries. [{adr}]

in_process_state.description: ADR-002 invariant: session state and token blacklists MUST never be stored in process memory. Flags module-level and class-level mutable containers whose name identifies them as session or token-revocation state, plus memoised session lookups.
in_process_state.message: {name} holds {detail} in process memory. ADR-002 invariant: session state and token blacklists MUST live in the shared Redis cache layer - an in-process container is lost the moment the pod is rescheduled. [{adr}]

self_test.description: run_all.py --self-test asserts the compliant tree is clean and that every rule listed here actually fires on the violating tree. It is how we prove the checks are not vacuous.
